question:
A 89-year-old woman presents with an 18-month history of gradually enlarging fingertips and a
2-month history of hoarseness. She reports decreased appetite following a respiratory infection 3
months ago and has experienced an 8-kg (17.6-lb) weight loss since then. She denies smoking. Her
medical history includes obstructive sleep apnea diagnosed 10 years ago, for which she uses a CPAP
mask at night. She appears fatigued, and her vital signs are normal. Physical examination reveals
increased convexity of the nail folds, painful swelling of the soft tissues of the fingers and ankles, and
faint wheezing in the right upper lung field. There is no discoloration of her lips or oral mucosa. This
patient’s condition is most likely associated with which of the following findings? Answer Choices: (A)
Bilateral pleural effusions (B) Bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy (C) Increased serum calcium
concentration (D) Decreased serum PTHrP levels (E) Elevated serum ACE levels (F) Reticular
opacities on chest x-ray (G) Clubbing of toenails only (H) Unilateral facial anhidrosis (I) Decreased
serum growth hormone levels (J) Peripheral cyanosis
 A. Increased serum calcium concentration
B. Peripheral cyanosis
C. Reticular opacities on chest x-ray
D. Bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy
E. Bilateral pleural effusions
F. Clubbing of toenails only
G. Elevated serum ACE levels
H. Decreased serum PTHrP levels
I. Unilateral facial anhidrosis
J. Decreased serum growth hormone levels
